stories.headline: Norwegian Royal Family in Crisis: Queen Sonja Hospitalized, Mette-Marit's Illness Worsens, King Harald Addresses Epstein Links
stories.summary: Norway's royal family faced a cascade of health emergencies and reputational challenges during the week. Queen Sonja, 88, was hospitalized for heart failure and atrial fibrillation before being discharged. Crown Prince Haakon publicly disclosed that Crown Princess Mette-Marit's pulmonary fibrosis is worsening and that she is 'gravely ill,' prompting him to cut a Japan trip short. King Harald, 89, spoke to press during his Vestland county tour, addressing all three health crises and defending Mette-Marit over renewed scrutiny of her past friendship with Jeffrey Epstein, stating she 'deserves credit' for breaking the connection early.

stories.headline: Norway Joins France's Nuclear Deterrence Initiative, Signs Bilateral Defence Pact; Russia Issues Warning
stories.summary: Prime Minister Støre travelled to Paris and signed the 'Narvik Agreement' with President Macron, making Norway the ninth country to join France's nuclear deterrence initiative and committing to mutual defence assistance, including discussion of how French nuclear weapons could strengthen European security. Russia issued a stark warning that the move 'will not go unanswered,' framing it as a threat to Russian national security. The agreement also covers hybrid warfare, maritime security, space cooperation, cybersecurity, and defence industry collaboration.

stories.headline: Barth Eide Named as Potential Ukraine Peace Envoy, Lays Out Norway's Position on Russia-Ukraine Negotiations
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide attended an informal EU foreign ministers meeting in Lemesos, Cyprus, where he argued that Europe should participate in Ukraine-Russia peace talks but not as a neutral mediator, given Europe's strong support for Ukraine. Barth Eide was himself named in Politico and Norwegian media as a potential candidate for a European peace envoy role. Norway separately pledged 425 million NOK to strengthen Ukraine's energy infrastructure.

Norwegian military attaché in Kyiv confirmed Norwegian personnel would remain in Ukraine despite Russian threats.

stories.summary: Prime Minister Støre and Children's Minister Lene Vågslid convened an emergency meeting at Kripos with police, PST, and child welfare agencies to discuss the rapid growth of violent online communities ('The Com' and similar networks) exploiting and radicalising Norwegian children and youth. Støre sharply criticised tech giants for failing to take responsibility, using notably strong language, and the government announced several new measures. Norwegian police had registered 73 criminal cases linked to these environments in the period.

stories.headline: Norway Presses EU to Drop Arctic Drilling Moratorium; New Norway-EU Engagement Strategy Outlined
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Barth Eide has sent nearly a dozen ministers to Brussels this year to pressure the EU into lifting its 2021 Arctic drilling moratorium, arguing there is no climate rationale for treating Arctic oil and gas differently. Barth Eide separately announced a new Norwegian strategy to engage earlier and more actively in EU policy development, positioning Norway as an informal influencer ('back-seat driver'). Former senior EEA official Maria Varteressian warned the EEA agreement is increasingly strained by geopolitical shifts. The EU Commission subsequently signalled it would ease emissions rules for oil and gas under Norwegian pressure.

stories.headline: FrP Approaches 30% in Polls, Listhaug Touted as Potential Prime Minister
stories.summary: Multiple May polls showed the Progress Party (FrP) approaching 30% support — nearly double that of the Conservative Party (Høyre) — fuelling speculation about Sylvi Listhaug's prospects as a future prime minister. FrP veteran Carl I. Hagen publicly predicted Støre's government could fall as early as autumn 2026. Listhaug remained active on multiple policy fronts, including an op-ed blaming the government's industrial policy for the Morrow battery factory collapse, a stir over immigration remarks by an FrP adviser, and a new party branch founding in Nordkapp.

stories.headline: Stortinget Defense Long-Term Plan Negotiations Stall; FrP Warns of Funding Crisis
stories.summary: Negotiations over Norway's revised Long-Term Defence Plan (LTP) continued without agreement in the Storting's Foreign Affairs and Defence Committee. FrP sounded the alarm that Forsvaret lacks funds for daily training and exercises, threatening to withhold support for a broad defence settlement. Defence Minister Tore O. Sandvik acknowledged major investments could crowd out operational expenditure but denied a crisis existed. Southern Norwegian county governors separately demanded greater defence allocations for their region in the new plan. Separately, Norway signed an intent agreement to procure Patria 6x6 armoured vehicles and Norway-Germany jointly promoted Type 212CD submarines to Canada at the CANSEC defence exhibition.

The proposal, included in the revised national budget request, drew sharp criticism from economists and analysts who labelled it speculation, 'gambling,' and 'magic' given the financial risks of the novel mechanism.

stories.summary: Stortinget budget negotiations for the revised national budget continued amid tensions between coalition and support parties. Commentators and opposition figures raised doubts about Labour's ability to deliver a stable budget, with MDG threatening to withdraw support over spending levels and Senterpartiet having earlier defected to push through fuel tax cuts. FrP Finance Minister challenger Stoltenberg faced opposition from FrP on food VAT policy. Public debate also touched on hospital underfunding and rising interest rate expectations from NAV vacancy data.
